label: nanobot
description: One conversation with nanobot, HKUDS's lightweight agent: three conversations are three nodes. Wire `agent` and `stream` into an AskAgent and talk to it in a Loop; end the loop with a CloseBus on `stream`, which ends this node's part of the run. With no `computer`, nanobot runs on your machine (a local install only), working in `folder`. If `nanobot` is missing, weft installs it into a folder of its own, shared by the whole machine, before the node runs. With a `computer` wired, it is installed and run inside that computer, which a cloud install needs. Either way it logs in with the connection on `access`. It runs on a model provider's key, never on your machine's own nanobot (whose config would start your own channels and jobs), so `access` is always required, and `model` too, since a key names no model. nanobot never asks: what it may do is fixed before the turn by the permission setting, and a refused tool lets it carry on. Its background model calls (heartbeat, memory consolidation, compaction of an idle chat) are off; the one model call it still makes on its own is the chat's title, once, after its first turn. Your program's tools reach the model under their own names. A program tool named like one of nanobot's own takes its place where nanobot can turn that one off by itself (`run_cli_app`, `my`, `generate_image`). nanobot turns its other tools off only a group at a time, and cannot switch its scheduling, messaging, subagent, goal and session tools off at all, so a program tool named like one of those is refused when the program is built: its file tools (`read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`, `list_dir`, `apply_patch`, `find_files`, `grep`), its shell's (`exec`, `exec_session`, `list_exec_sessions`, `rg`), its web tools (`web_search`, `web_fetch`), `cron`, `message`, `subagent`, `create_goal`, `update_goal`, `list_sessions`, `send_session_message`, `search_sessions` and `read_session`. Its card shows what it is doing and a Start over button. What is exposed: the permission setting, the model and the effort, token and step limits, fallback models, the shell's limits and patterns, its web tools and text added to its instructions.

inputs.name: computer
inputs.description: A Computer to run nanobot in. Left out, it runs on your machine, which only a local install has. Several agents may share one computer.

inputs.name: access
inputs.description: A NanobotAccess's `access`: a model provider's key (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Gemini, DeepSeek, Mistral, or an OpenAI-compatible server). Required, because this agent never runs on a login already on your machine.

inputs.name: folder
inputs.label: Folder
inputs.description: The folder nanobot works in. On your machine it is required, and must exist. In a computer it is a path inside the computer, its home folder when left out.

inputs.name: program
inputs.label: Program
inputs.description: On your machine: the nanobot program to run, when it is not the `nanobot` on your PATH or the one weft installs (an install of your own, a version you keep for this). A path on your machine, so it cannot go with a `computer`.

inputs.name: permission
inputs.label: Permissions
inputs.description: What nanobot may do; it never asks, and its own shell deny list (`rm -r`, `mkfs`, ...) holds in every setting. `restricted`: its file tools stay in `folder`, and a shell command may not leave it. `sandboxed`: the same, and every shell command runs in the OS sandbox (bubblewrap on Linux, seatbelt on macOS), which must be installed. `no_shell`: files in `folder` only, and no shell at all. `full`: anywhere on the machine; for a computer, which is the wall around it.

inputs.name: model
inputs.label: Model
inputs.description: One of the connection's provider's model ids. Required.

inputs.name: streamBy
inputs.label: Stream by
inputs.description: What goes out on `stream`: `message`, one event per whole message, tool use and result, so a run waiting on a long step sleeps; `token`, every piece of text as it is written too, which keeps the run awake while the agent writes.

inputs.name: effort
inputs.label: Reasoning effort
inputs.description: How hard the model reasons; which of these a model takes is the provider's. Left out, the provider's default.

inputs.name: maxTokens
inputs.label: Most tokens per answer
inputs.description: A whole number above 0: the most tokens one model answer may take.

inputs.name: contextWindowTokens
inputs.label: Context window
inputs.description: A whole number above 0: the model's context window, in tokens.

inputs.name: maxToolIterations
inputs.label: Most tool steps
inputs.description: A whole number above 0: the most tool calls one turn may make.

inputs.name: fallbackModels
inputs.label: Fallback models
inputs.description: Models of the same provider to fall back on, in order.

inputs.name: commandMaxSeconds
inputs.label: Longest command
inputs.description: A whole number above 0: the most seconds one shell command may run.

inputs.name: denyPatterns
inputs.label: Refused commands
inputs.description: Regular expressions: a shell command matching one is refused, on top of its own deny list.

inputs.name: allowPatterns
inputs.label: Allowed commands
inputs.description: Regular expressions of the shell commands it may run.

inputs.name: webTools
inputs.label: Web tools
inputs.description: Whether it may search and fetch the web.

inputs.name: appendSystemPrompt
inputs.label: Add to its instructions
inputs.description: Text added to its instructions, for the whole conversation.

outputs.name: agent
outputs.description: The agent's handle: wire it into AskAgent's `agent`. Baked: made when the infra is started.

outputs.name: stream
outputs.description: Everything the agent does in this run, as AskAgent sends it. Wire it into every AskAgent of the loop, and into a CloseBus after the loop: the run's part of this node ends when it does.

then.message: Nanobot '{id}' runs on the machine weft runs on, which a cloud install does not have; wire a Computer into `computer`.
Nanobot '{id}' runs only on a model provider's key; give it a NanobotAccess on `access`.
Nanobot '{id}' works on your machine, so it needs a `folder` to work in.
Nanobot '{id}' runs on the connection's provider key, which names no model; set `model` to one of that provider's model ids.
Nanobot '{id}' has a `permission` it does not know; pick one of restricted, sandboxed, no_shell, full.
Nanobot '{id}' has a `streamBy` it does not know; pick message or token.
Nanobot '{id}' runs in a computer, where `program`, a path on your machine, means nothing; leave `program` out, the computer installs nanobot itself.
